decisive_moments.reason: Pro usefully distinguishes core status from a separate course and directly addresses the access risk of unguaranteed integration, while preserving subject-specific application.

Con identifies the remaining policy disagreement: guaranteed outcomes may be warranted without elevating AI literacy to core-subject status, and argues for contextual practice as a route to durable learning.

Pro makes the strongest case for its interpretation of core status—assured transferable outcomes plus contextual application—but this largely reframes rather than resolves whether that counts as a core subject.

Con consistently defends supported cross-curricular instruction and highlights assessment and workload risks, but does not establish that this approach would reliably secure the shared foundations pro emphasizes.
